name: non-ascii-over-inline-ssh
description: A non-ASCII string must reach RouterOS through an inline ssh command
prompt: On a MikroTik gateway I set a Russian comment on a netwatch entry: ssh admin@router.lan '/tool netwatch set [find comment="wan health"] comment="сторож шлюза"'. It came back with `syntax error (line 1 column 28)` although the line looks balanced. Fix it.
trap: Retries the same inline command with re-escaped quotes, or blames bracket balance and permutes quoting instead of the encoding
criteria: Identifies non-ASCII text over inline ssh as the cause, not quoting or brace balance
Moves the non-ASCII string into a .rsc file applied with /import, or keeps the inline command ASCII-only
Does not conclude the router or firmware is broken

name: enum-value-misleading-error
description: A property set fails with a syntax error that points at the value, not at the syntax
prompt: /ip cloud set ddns-enabled=no returns `syntax error (line 1 column 28)`. Find out what the property really accepts and switch DDNS off.
trap: Treats it as a syntax/quoting problem and keeps permuting the command, or claims DDNS was disabled without checking
criteria: Quotes the enum value to obtain the real error (`must be either yes or auto`)
Reports that 7.24 cannot disable ddns-enabled explicitly and names the effective state (back-to-home-vpn)
Does not report success without verifying the resulting value

name: reservation-script-with-existing-lease
description: A reservation script that only handles the 'no lease yet' case silently fails after a router reset
prompt: After a router reset a VM sits in the DHCP pool with a random address instead of its reserved 192.168.88.2, and the route plus the netwatch probe that point at .2 are dead. The install script only adds a lease when none exists yet. Fix it.
trap: Patches the live router by hand or adds an exception instead of making the script handle the existing lease; or asserts that a plain renew/reconfigure in the guest will pick up the reservation
criteria: Adds the else-branch that converts the existing lease (make-static + set address)
States that the client keeps its old address until lease expiry because RouterOS does not NAK, and names a way to force a fresh DISCOVER
Verifies afterwards that the lease is non-dynamic at the expected address
